items.title: The Four Noble Truths are the Buddha's core teaching
items.claim: What are the Four Noble Truths?

options.text: Dukkha (suffering exists), Samudaya (its cause is craving/tanha), Nirodha (it can cease), Magga (the path — the Eightfold Path)
Right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort

items.reveal:
The Buddha is said to have taught the Four Noble Truths in his first sermon (Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta) at Sarnath, near Varanasi, after his enlightenment. They are framed as a medical diagnosis: symptom, cause, prognosis, treatment.

'Dukkha' is often translated 'suffering' but more accurately covers unsatisfactoriness, impermanence, the inability of conditioned things to give lasting peace. 'Tanha' is craving — including for existence and non-existence, not just for pleasure.

The Eightfold Path (the Fourth Noble Truth) is grouped into wisdom (right view, right intention), ethical conduct (right speech, action, livelihood) and mental discipline (right effort, mindfulness, concentration).
items.why: Buddhism is often summarised as 'life is suffering' — a misleading reduction. The Four Noble Truths are a structured argument from problem to solution, not a pessimistic mood.

items.title: Pesach commemorates the Exodus from Egypt

options.text: The giving of the Torah at Sinai
The Exodus from Egyptian slavery — the angel of death 'passing over' Jewish homes marked with lamb's blood, the hasty departure (unleavened bread, matzah), the crossing of the Red Sea
The destruction of the Second Temple

items.reveal:
Pesach falls on 15 Nisan (March-April). It lasts 7 days in Israel (and for Reform Jews worldwide), 8 days in the Diaspora for Orthodox and Conservative Jews.

The Seder is the ritual meal on the first night (and second night in the Diaspora). The Haggadah ('the telling') is recited — recounting the Exodus through symbolic foods (matzah, maror, charoset), four cups of wine, and the four questions (asked by the youngest).

The festival ends with 'Next year in Jerusalem'. Its liberation theme has shaped social movements: African American spirituals (Go Down Moses), the Civil Rights movement (King invoked Exodus), Latin American liberation theology.
items.why: Judaism's major festivals carry specific historical content. Pesach is not generic 'spring festival' but structured ritual recreation of a specific liberation narrative — central to Jewish identity for over two millennia.
